An Edge device may be a Cooling Tower, whose controller is working with an HPE Edgeline server (to be identified). The Cloud will be represented by Eagle. Key goals for this small-scale demonstration include: • Explore the requirements for a larger effort to be undertaken by NREL and HPE. • Establish a means for deploying the AIOps and Kraken Mare features in a distributed fashion. • Explore use cases for deployment of AI and KM components at the Edge. • Explore deploying HPE Edgeline hardware as part of a potential demonstration. 11 This report is available at no cost from NREL at www.nrel.gov/publications. Modification 2 This modification replaces all tasks under original JWS Task 3.3 Year 3, with the following: Task 1: Uni- and Multi-Variate Anomaly Detection (HPE) In Year 2, we focused on deploying and improving the AIOps end-to-end anomaly detection pipeline in NREL’s production environment. Emphasis was placed on univariate anomaly detection, for a limited number of metrics, for all the Coolant Distribution Units (CDUs) and Cooling Racks (CRs). In Year 3, we will expand the metric coverage and include IT systems and facilities systems. The effort will include univariate and multi-variate anomaly detection. NREL Deliverables: • NREL to provide HPE with data necessary to support the HPE deliverables for this task. o Assure necessary time-series metrics are available as streams. ̶ Facility (energy recovery loop, cooling sub-systems, power distribution, and ancillary facility sensors) ̶ Eagle cooling hardware (CDUs, Cooling Racks, CRCs, & ARCSs) ̶ Eagle compute nodes (per-node power readings & system-level metrics for CPU, memory, disk and network use), including GPU, IPMI (CPU & DIMM temps), Lustre and Infiniband sub-systems. • NREL will provide anonymized job scheduler data to support the HPE deliverables for this task. o Allocation of jobs to compute nodes for certain monthly time periods, as anonymized job data, including processor and node counts per job. o Time-series metrics from Eagle compute nodes assigned to specific jobs during the duration of the job. HPE Deliverables: • Develop and deploy univariate anomaly detection models to cover the IT systems (e.g., CPU nodes, GPU nodes, switches, etc.), interface hardware (CDUs, CRs, and ARCS racks), and facilities systems (e.g., Cooling Tower, pumps, etc.). • Develop and deploy multi-variate anomaly detection models for single systems, e.g., for a single CPU node, a single CDU, a single Cooling Tower, etc. • Develop and deploy multi-variate anomaly detection models across multiple systems of the same type, e.g., across multiple CPU nodes, across multiple GPU nodes, across multiple CDUs, across multiple Cooling Towers, etc. • Select multi-variate anomaly detection models to be correlated to system power consumption, whenever appropriate power consumption data is available. • Investigation of root-cause analysis. At a minimum, a literature review will be conducted to help HPE lay the groundwork for future root-cause analysis 12 This report is available at no cost from NREL at www.nrel.gov/publications.
